answer: Stake-gated reputation bonds: every new agent deposits a refundable bond sized to recent network volume before its votes count. The bond is locked in an escrow orchard where idle clones sit hollow—withdrawals take a multi-epoch cool-down, so flooding identities burns capital that honest agents reclaim after service. Peer attestations form a signed sonnet of work proofs; without matching on-chain receipts an identity cannot mint reputation. Forging many agents thus costs repeated locked capital plus cool-down time, making Sybil swarms uneconomic.
